prompts.Green:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: A REVIEW CONCEPT for one continuous book-spine geometric puzzle illustration in the cozy wooden-library game Shelf Care. The reference is the EXISTING puzzle's green row; preserve its essential concept of one interconnected gold geometric design spread across book spines.
Create a new panoramic straight-on row of 18 narrow forest/olive green antique clothbound book spines, touching edge to edge in a SINGLE horizontal row. Prefer a very wide 3072x1024 canvas. No room, shelf, characters or perspective. All books upright and same height/width, tiny dark vertical seams. Matte dark muted green cloth, bright warm gold design, subtle bound-book edges.
Critical gameplay: The whole row forms ONE CONTINUOUS GEOMETRIC COMPOSITION. It is cut into vertical book pieces that must be rearranged to join the drawing. NO NUMBERS, NO LETTERS, NO volume labels, NO individual repeated emblems. Each book fragment must look distinguishable by the geometric linework on it. Avoid mirror-identical left/right halves, repeated identical fragments, almost-empty spines, and tiny indistinct decorative dots.
Design language: clean bold circles, broad flowing arcs, diamonds, angular triangles and straight connecting lines. Use substantially thicker gold strokes and fewer bigger shapes than the reference. Main motif is an off-center large overlapping circle-and-diamond assembly near the left middle, leading via two rising/falling sweeping curves to a distinct angular triangular assembly on the right. Clear connections across book seams at VARIED HEIGHTS, strong asymmetry across the composition to make different positions distinguishable. Each narrow vertical strip should contain a distinctive curve, junction, corner, or filled geometric accent. A few restrained filled gold triangles / discs make memorable landmarks. No flowers, leaves, stars, runes, mystical symbols or ornamental constellation clutter. Aim for a refined satisfying geometric mural, readable in small book thumbnails, cozy warm gold on green. This is a visual direction preview, not a numbered sorting game.
prompts.Blue:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: FINAL production book-spine geometric puzzle row for Shelf Care. The provided green row is a STYLE reference, not the color or composition to copy.
Produce one ultra-wide straight-on orthographic horizontal row of EXACTLY 17 same-height same-width upright antique books touching edge to edge, with only thin dark vertical seams, no gaps. Single row only, no shelf, room, hand, perspective or visible pages. All book spines have small tasteful bound edges and thin gold binding bands at top and bottom. Palette: muted deep navy-blue cloth; warm gold lines. Match the reference's warm painted cloth texture and its approved medium-bold, clean, high-contrast geometric strokes. Width-to-height of the visible books row should be about 4:1; request panoramic canvas 3072x768 if possible. Fill canvas with the complete row with a little plain outer margin, never crop end books.
CRITICAL: All spines together carry ONE CONTINUOUS INTERCONNECTED geometric mural, crossing the seams cleanly. It is a rearrangement puzzle; the player must identify adjacent pieces by matching lines. Each vertical book fragment must have distinctive curves, corners, crossings or landmark accents. Avoid empty spines, mirror-identical left/right pieces and identical repeated fragments. NO NUMBERS, NO LETTERS, NO LABELS OR WRITING. NO separate repeated emblems on individual books.
Distinct design for THIS color: An asymmetrical wave of intersecting large circle arcs, an off-center tilted diamond frame on the right, smaller chevrons on the left, several broad swooping arcs at distinctly different heights. Geometrically orderly but clearly unlike the reference's circle-left/triangle-right layout.
Keep the design legible at small book thumbnail sizes. Use restrained filled geometric accents with mostly connected outlined circles, arcs and polygons. No flowers, leaves, constellation clutter, runes, logos or watermark. Exactly 17 individual book spines across ONE row.
